## Goals for Today

::::: columns
::: {.column width="\"50%"}
-   Come back to the general structure of `ggplot2`.
-   Learn a few standard graphs for numerical/quantitative data:
    -   **Histogram**: one numerical variable
    -   **Side-by-side boxplot**: one numerical variable and one categorical variable
    -   **Side-by-side violin plot**: one numerical variable and one categorical variable
    -   **Scatterplot**: two numerical variables
    -   **Linegraph**: two numerical variables
:::

::: {.column width="\"50%"}
-   And, learn the standard graphic for categorical data:
    -   **Barplot**: one categorical variable
    -   **Segmented barplot**: two categorical variables
-   Also cover some common extensions and customizations.
:::
:::::

## `ggplot2` example code

**Guiding Principle**: We will map variables from the **data** to the **aes**thetic attributes (e.g. location, size, shape, color) of **geom**etric objects (e.g. points, lines, bars).

<br>

```{r, eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
ggplot(data = ---, mapping = aes(---)) +
  geom_---(---) 
```

<br>

Will add in other layers today, such as:

-   `scales_---_---()`

-   `labs()`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Histograms

```{r, eval = FALSE, tidy = FALSE}
ggplot(data = ---, mapping = aes(---)) +
  geom_---(---) 
```

```{r hist2}
#| output-location: column

# Create histogram
ggplot(data = july_2019, 
       mapping = aes(x = Total)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "white",
                 fill = "violetred1",
                 bins = 50)
```

-   **mapping** to a variable goes in `aes()` and **setting** to a specific value goes in the `geom_---()`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Boxplots {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **Five number summary**:
    -   Minimum
    -   First quartile (Q1)
    -   Median
    -   Third quartile (Q3)
    -   Maximum
-   Interquartile range (IQR) $=$ Q3 $-$ Q1
-   Outliers: **unusual** points
    -   Boxplot defines unusual as being beyond $1.5*IQR$ from $Q1$ or $Q3$.
-   Whiskers: reach out to the furthest point that is NOT an outlier
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data = july_2019, 
       mapping = aes(x = Occasion, 
                     y = Total)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
:::
:::::

## Linegraphs

Also called **time series plot** when time is represented on the x axis.

```{r}
#| output-location: column

ggplot(data = july_2019,
       mapping = aes(x = Time,
                     y = Total,
                     color = Occasion)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Linegraphs

Also called **time series plot** when time is represented on the x axis.

```{r}
#| output-location: column


ggplot(data = july_2019,
       mapping = aes(x = Time,
                     y = Total,
                     color = Occasion)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme(legend.position= "bottom")
```

## New Data Setting: [NFL 2018 Game Outcomes](https://data.scorenetwork.org/football/nfl-game-outcomes.html)

```{r}
nfl_outcomes_2018 <- read_csv("https://data.scorenetwork.org/data/nfl_mahomes_era_games.csv")
glimpse(nfl_outcomes_2018)


```

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

phi_buf <- filter(nfl_outcomes_2018, home_team %in% c("PHI", "BUF") | 
                   away_team %in% c("PHI", "BUF")) %>%
  mutate(playing = case_when(home_team == "PHI" & away_team != "BUF" ~ "PHI only",
                             home_team == "PHI" & away_team == "BUF" ~ "Both",
                             home_team != "PHI" & away_team == "BUF" ~ "BUF only",
                             home_team == "BUF" & away_team == "PHI" ~ "Both",
                             home_team == "BUF" & away_team != "PHI" ~ "BUF only",
                             home_team != "BUF" & away_team == "PHI" ~ "PHI only",
                             ))
count(phi_buf, playing)


buf <- filter(nfl_outcomes_2018, home_team == "BUF" | away_team == "BUF") %>%
  mutate(where = if_else(home_team == "BUF", "home", "away"))

ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = game_type)) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = game_type, fill = where)) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = where, fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar()

ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = where, fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge")

ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = where, fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +

ggplot(data = buf,
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Segmented Barplots

```{r}
#| output-location: column

# Create segmented barplot
ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = where,
                     fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

-   Each bar is divided into the frequencies of the `fill` variable.

-   Hard to make comparisons across categories.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Segmented Barplots

```{r}
#| output-location: column


# Create segmented barplot
ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = where,
                     fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

-   Can add the `position` argument into the `geom_bar()`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Segmented Barplots

```{r}
#| output-location: column


# Create segmented barplot
ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = where,
                     fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

-   Now each bar is divided into **proportions** based on the `fill` variable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Segmented Barplots

```{r}
#| output-location: column


# Create segmented barplot
ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(fill = where,
                     x = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

-   How does our interpretation of the segmented change when we swap the variable mappings?

## Adding More Variables

-   Two main approaches:
    -   Utilize other `aes`thetics of the `geom`
    -   Facet: Create multiple plots across the categories of a categorical variable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Utilize other `aes`thetics

The basic `geom_boxplot()` needs an `x` and a `y` aesthetic:

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = as.factor(game_outcome),
                     y = score_diff)) +
  geom_boxplot() 
```

But you can also add `color` to get another categorical variable on the graph.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Utilize other `aes`thetics

The basic `geom_boxplot()` needs an `x` and a `y` aesthetic:

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = as.factor(game_outcome),
                     y = score_diff, 
                     fill = where)) +
  geom_boxplot() 
```

But you can also add `color` to get another categorical variable on the graph.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Facet

```{r}
#| output-location: column

ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = where,
                     fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  facet_wrap(~game_type)

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Facet

```{r, fig.asp = 1.25}
#| output-location: column


ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = where,
                     fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  facet_grid(week~game_type)
```

Let's fix the over-crowded y axis tick marks!

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Facet

```{r, fig.asp = 1.25}
#| output-location: column


ggplot(data = buf, 
       mapping = aes(x = where,
                     fill = as.factor(game_outcome))) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  facet_grid(week~game_type) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 3))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Adding Some Context

```{r line3}
#| output-location: column

buf <- mutate(buf, 
              outcome = if_else(game_outcome == 1,
                                "Won", "Lost"))

ggplot(data = buf,
       mapping = aes(x = outcome,
                     y = score_diff, 
                     fill = where)) +
  geom_boxplot()  +
  labs(x = "Outcome of the Game",
       y = "Difference in Score Between \nWinner and Loser",
       color = "Where was the Game?",
       caption = "Data from the nflreadr Package",
       title = "The Buffalo Bills Should Only Play At Home.")
```

## Customizing your `ggplot2` Plots

-   There are so **many** ways you can customize the look of your `ggplot2` plots.

-   Let's look at some common changes:

    -   Fussing with labels
    -   Removing the legend
    -   Zooming in
    -   Using multiple `geoms`
    -   Color!
    -   Themes

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Fussing with Labels: Rotate

```{r bar4}
#| output-location: column

# Focus on games outside the regular season
buf_not_reg <- filter(buf, game_type != "REG")

ggplot(data = buf_not_reg,
       mapping = aes(x = game_id,
                     y = score_diff)) +
  geom_col()

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Fussing with Labels: Rotate

```{r bar5}
#| output-location: column

# Focus on games outside the regular season
buf_not_reg <- filter(buf, game_type != "REG")

ggplot(data = buf_not_reg,
       mapping = aes(x = game_id,
                     y = score_diff)) +
  geom_col() + 
  theme(axis.text.x =
          element_text(angle = 45,
                       vjust = 1,
                       hjust = 1))

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Not Including a Legend

```{r bar6}
#| output-location: column

# Focus on games outside the regular season
buf_not_reg <- filter(buf, game_type != "REG")

ggplot(data = buf_not_reg,
       mapping = aes(x = game_id,
                     y = score_diff,
                     fill = outcome)) +
  geom_col() + 
  theme(axis.text.x =
          element_text(angle = 45,
                       vjust = 1,
                       hjust = 1)) +
  guides(fill = "none")

```

## Zooming In

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = july_2019, 
       mapping = aes(x = Occasion, 
                     y = Total,
                     fill = Occasion)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  guides(fill = "none")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Zooming In

```{r box5}
#| output-location: column

ggplot(data = july_2019, 
       mapping = aes(x = Occasion, 
                     y = Total,
                     fill = Occasion)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 40))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Including Multiple `geom`s

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = july_2019, 
       mapping = aes(x = Occasion, 
                     y = Total,
                     fill = Occasion)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 40)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1,
              height = 0, 
              alpha = 0.6)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Including Multiple `geom`s

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = july_2019,
       mapping = aes(x = Time,
                     y = Total,
                     color = Occasion)) +
  geom_line(size = 2) +
  theme(legend.position= "bottom") +
  geom_point(size = 3)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Changing the Color

```{r}
colors()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Changing the Color

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = july_2019,
       mapping = aes(x = Time,
                     y = Total,
                     color = Occasion)) +
  geom_line(size = 2) +
  theme(legend.position= "bottom") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("violetred2",
                                "steelblue4"))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Changing the Color

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = july_2019,
       mapping = aes(x = Time,
                     y = Total,
                     color = Occasion)) +
  geom_line(size = 2) +
  theme(legend.position= "bottom") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#0D6759",
                                "#E4844A"))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Using a [Different Theme](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggtheme.html)

```{r}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = july_2019,
       mapping = aes(x = Time,
                     y = Total,
                     color = Occasion)) +
  geom_line(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#0D6759",
                                "#E4844A")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position= "bottom")
```
